properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 3:41AM PST until November 21 at 11:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM
today and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
